metadata.title: Acme Health Patient Intake API — CGE-P Capstone Component

components.title: acme-health-intake
components.description: The Acme Health patient intake API: S3 uploads bucket, DynamoDB submissions table, Lambda handler, and API Gateway HTTP API, hardened against the eight named gaps in GAPS.md and governed under a CMMC Level 2 / NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3 control selection.
components.purpose: Accept and store patient intake submissions (PHI) with encryption, access control, and audit controls appropriate for a CMMC Level 2 scope.

control-implementations.description: Implementation of NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3 (CMMC Level 2) controls satisfied by this system, mapped to the eight named gaps in GAPS.md.

implemented-requirements.description: GAP-01 CLOSED. The uploads bucket is encrypted with SSE-KMS using a customer-managed key (aws_kms_key.s3), reused from the KMS key provisioned for the primary/log buckets rather than a dedicated key. GAP-02 is also closed under this same control: the DynamoDB submissions table specifies server_side_encryption with the same customer-managed key rather than the AWS-owned default.

implemented-requirements.description: GAP-07 CLOSED. The Lambda's inline IAM policy is scoped to exactly the actions the handler performs (dynamodb:PutItem, s3:PutObject, plus kms:Decrypt/kms:GenerateDataKey required once DynamoDB's encryption moved to a customer-managed key), replacing the original dynamodb:* / s3:* wildcard grants.

implemented-requirements.description: GAP-08 PARTIALLY CLOSED. The API Gateway default stage has access_log_settings (CloudWatch) and default_route_settings (throttling) configured. The WAF portion of this control is NOT implemented: AWS WAFv2 does not support direct association with HTTP APIs (aws_apigatewayv2_*) — only REST APIs (v1), ALB, Cognito, AppSync, and App Runner. Migrating to a REST API or fronting the HTTP API with CloudFront would be required to close this fully, both out of scope for this capstone. Compensating controls: API Gateway's own throttling limits, CloudWatch access logging, and AWS Security Hub (FSBP + NIST 800-53 standards) monitoring the account.

implemented-requirements.description: GAP-05 NOT IMPLEMENTED — accepted risk. The intake Lambda is not deployed inside the starter's VPC. Closing this gap requires a NAT Gateway so the private subnets (which currently have no route to AWS services) can reach DynamoDB, S3, CloudWatch Logs, and SQS from within the VPC. A NAT Gateway carries a real ongoing hourly cost, which was deemed out of scope for this capstone's timeline and budget. Compensating controls: the Lambda's IAM role is already scoped to least privilege (see 03.01.05 above), and AWS Security Hub continuously monitors the account for related findings. Detection policy (compliance.gap05_aws) is written and unit-tested but intentionally excluded from the CI enforcement gate, since enforcing an unimplemented control would permanently block merges.

GAP-06 NOT IMPLEMENTED — accepted risk. The intake Lambda has no reserved concurrency, dead-letter queue, or active X-Ray tracing. This was deferred for the same reason as 03.13.01 (GAP-05): a DLQ and CloudWatch logging both depend on the same VPC network path a NAT Gateway would provide, so this was scoped out alongside GAP-05. Compensating controls: Lambda's built-in retry behavior on invocation errors, and Security Hub monitoring. Detection policy (compliance.gap06_aws) is written and unit-tested but intentionally excluded from the CI enforcement gate.
